newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money needs down, gilts continue rise.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money needs down, gilts continue rise.

text.p: Indian call money rates fell on good liquidity to end Wednesday at 2.0-2.25 percent against opening quotes of 3.0-3.5 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was done between 2.75 percent and 3.25 percent and rates fell in the afternoon on lack of demand.
Dealers said the supply of funds was good and would keep call money rates at current levels till excess liquidity was sucked out of the system through a bond issue.
They said they expected the government to announce an issue in the next few days, given the easy money conditions.
Government security prices rose in brisk trade driven by low call money rates, dealers said. Prices have risen in the past four days on demand fuelled by easy call money.
The 12.59 percent 2004 government of India stock traded on Wednesday between 101.33 and 101.40 rupees against Tuesday's 101.06 and 101.27, dealers said.
The 12.14 percent 2000 traded between 102.15 and 102.19 against Tuesday's 102.15 while the 13.50 percent 1998 rose to 103.57 from 103.50, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in April 1998 yielded 8.2-8.3 percent while July bills yielded 8.4-8.5 percent, they said.
